newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity eases after hitting some highs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity eases after hitting some highs.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures eased Wednesday in a late sell off after some front months hit new contract highs, industry sources said.
"It was a big run up," one broker said of power futures price increases this week, adding "we're selling it back off."
November California Oregon Border (COB) settled down 10 cents at $19.40 per megawatt hour (MWh) after meeting resistance at a new contract high of $20.05, the brokers said.
December COB ended down 37 cents at $20.23 after reaching a new contract high of $21.00, while January closed down eight cents at $19.07 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds from March, 1997 onward settled between 10 and 25 cents higher.
November Palo Verde finished down 15 cents at $18.45 per MWh after meeting resistance at a new contract high of $19.00, while December finished down 30 cents at $18.55 after trade as high as $18.80.
Remaining PV deferreds finished steady to 45 cents lower.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 263 COB and 178 PV contracts traded Wednesday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
